question: Why did the 4 h endpoint replay (seed 9002) show more false alarms than the seed-11 test split?
method: Regenerate the seed-11 test runs (runs 27-35, epochs from 1,800,000,000) and score v7's logged booster three ways, then count false alarms and warned breaches per scenario plan group.

paths.A_test_path: training/test rows: feature_rows every 5 s, rows inside a breach dropped, each run's random maintenance age
paths.B_replay_path_run_age: replay_rows (the scorer's path: build_features on the last 120 s every 5 s, in-breach rows scored), each run's maintenance age
paths.C_replay_path_catalog_age: replay_rows with the catalog maintenance age, as the endpoint replay and the live scorer use (clipped to 3000 h at these epochs)

finding: A vs B: the feature window, 5 s cadence, hysteresis, buffer and sample rate agree; false alarms and warnings are identical. The replay has more alert EPISODES because it also scores rows inside a breach (the test path drops them), so an alert can clear and reopen during a breach or cool-down. Those episodes are not false alarms (they open inside a breach).

B vs C: the difference is hours_since_maintenance. Training drew it at random per run (0-3000 h) although the simulated producer has no wear, and the trees learned a spurious dependence. At the replay epochs the catalog age is clipped to 3000 h, the edge of that range: false alarms +42 %, weak-precursor warnings halve. That, plus an alarm-heavy 4 h sample (13 false-alarm cycles vs ~7 expected), explains the replay gap.

Fix: live-format training rows now pin hours_since_maintenance to 3000 h (a constant column is never split on, and older versions see the same value on test and replay); the gate pools the test split with a fresh 12 h replay on the scorer path.

spot_check_v4_vs_v7_test_false_alarms.note: Both have 12 false alarms on the seed-11 test runs, but at different times: a coincidence of counts on the same fade/bump cycles, not a shared scoring bug.
